public_rationale: The factual premise is true. Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (e1), a project carrying a roughly $18bn construction loan (e3). The rest of the claim is hedged inference and opinion. He says the notice 'suggests' the OpenAI sites are materially behind schedule. He says Oracle is 'making sounds like' it won't pay its debts. He calls the notice 'beyond abnormal'. None of these comes with a test. Scoring them as facts would grade something he did not assert. For context, Oracle says the notice does not establish a delay (e2). The power pipeline has slipped to February 2027 (e2). And Oracle reportedly still covers the project's debt costs while the notice defers rent (e3). These points cut both ways but cannot settle a hedged inference.
limitations: Only the factual premise could be checked. It holds.
A companion statement in the same post asserts flatly that every Stargate site is heavily behind schedule. That is a separate, scorable claim and was not graded here.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Oracle's force majeure notice suggests its $340 billion of OpenAI data centers are materially behind schedule, and Oracle signals it may not pay its debts.

statement.excerpt: It is beyond abnormal for a company backing an $18 billion data center project to give a “force majeure” notice no matter what it says on Twitter, and suggests that the $340 billion in data centers it’s building for OpenAI are materially behind schedule, on top of the fact that Oracle is making sounds like it doesn’t intend to pay its debts, which is extremely alarming!

from_speaker: a company backing an $18 billion data center project
suggests that the $340 billion in data centers it's building for OpenAI are materially behind schedule
Oracle is making sounds like it doesn't intend to pay its debts
our_interpretation: The checkable premise is that Oracle sent a force majeure notice on a data center project tied to about $18bn of financing. That is a fact and is confirmed below.

The rest of the claim is hedged inference and characterization. 'Beyond abnormal' is an opinion. The notice 'suggests' delays across the portfolio. Oracle is 'making sounds like' it won't pay. He does not assert as fact that the $340bn portfolio is behind schedule or that Oracle will default. Testing those as established facts would score something he did not say.
No fixed period is scored. For context, the relevant window runs from the notice (2026-09-24) to the post (2026-10-06).
criteria.support_condition: Not scorable. The substantive parts are framed as what the notice 'suggests' and what Oracle is 'making sounds like', with no test for the inference.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scorable for the same reason.
